mainTopic: Whether a שכיב מרע can give gifts by speech alone: the stories of the בני רוכל and the man from מרון, רבי לוי's ruling on a קנין on שבת, and the משנה's dispute about שבת versus weekdays.
overview: The amud opens with the end of a משנה. The חכמים bring the case of the mother of the בני רוכל, a sick woman whose spoken gift of a brooch was upheld. רבי אליעזר brushes this off with a curse on her sons. In a ברייתא, רבי אליעזר tells his own story about a man from מרון who could give away his movables only along with land. The חכמים reply that this man was healthy, so his case proves nothing about a שכיב מרע. The גמרא explains that רבי אליעזר cursed the בני רוכל because they kept thorns in a vineyard, which he holds makes it forbidden as כלאים, since in ערביא thorns are grown for camels. רבי לוי rules that a קנין may be done for a dying man even on שבת, to keep him calm. A new משנה follows, with רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע arguing about whether a dying man's words count on שבת and on weekdays, and about acquiring for a minor or an adult. The גמרא says the משנה follows רבי יהודה, and it begins quoting רבי מאיר's opposite report of רבי אליעזר. That report continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The חכמים' proof from the mother of the בני רוכל
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים prove from a real case that a dying person's gift by speech alone is valid: a sick mother's brooch was given to her daughter just by her words.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: There was a case with the mother of the בני רוכל. She was sick and said, 'Give my brooch to my daughter,' and it was worth twelve hundred. She died, and they carried out what she said!
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים argue against רבי אליעזר, who says even a שכיב מרע needs a formal קנין. They bring a real-life case to prove him wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sick mother made no קנין at all. She just spoke, and the court still upheld her gift. So it looks like a dying person's words alone are enough, against רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: A real-life incident, brought as proof
A brooch or piece of jewelry
They upheld her words, meaning they carried out her instructions

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּאִמָּן שֶׁל בְּנֵי רוֹכֵל
phrases.english: They said to him: There was an incident with the mother of the sons of Rokhel
phrases.notes: "Him" is רבי אליעזר, who holds that even a dying person needs a proper קנין.

phrases.english: who was sick, and she said:
"Give my brooch to my daughter,
and it is worth twelve maneh,"
phrases.notes: A מנה is 100 דינרים, so the brooch was worth 1,200.

phrases.english: and she died, and they upheld her words!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּאִמָּן שֶׁל בְּנֵי רוֹכֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this section; continues the משנה's debate between רבי אליעזר and the חכמים.
steps.raayaObject: That a שכיב מרע can give gifts by speech alone, without a קנין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of the mother of the בני רוכל, whose spoken gift of a brooch was upheld.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר brushes off the proof with a curse
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר answers with a curse on the בני רוכל, hinting that this case was special and proves nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: The בני רוכל, may their mother bury them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר rejects the חכמים' proof. Instead of a long argument, he curses the sons, hinting that the case was unusual because of who they were.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He doesn't argue the law here. He points to the sons themselves, suggesting the ruling was shaped by their bad behavior and isn't the normal rule. The גמרא will soon ask what they did wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: May their mother bury them, a curse that they should die before her

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a story about burial. It is a curse, and the reason for it is explained later, in Steps 6 to 8.

phrases.english: He said to them:
The sons of Rokhel, may their mother bury them.
phrases.notes: A curse: may they die while their mother is still alive to bury them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: בְּנֵי רוֹכֵל – תִּקְבְּרֵם אִמָּן
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the case of the בני רוכל as a proof for the general law.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case was special because of the sons, so it cannot teach the normal rule.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's own story begins: the man from מרון
steps.stepSummary: In a ברייתא, רבי אליעזר tells of a man from מרון who wanted to give away movables and was told he could only do it by attaching them to land.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי אליעזר said to the חכמים: There was a man from מרון in ירושלים who had a lot of movable property and wanted to give it away as gifts. They told him: There is no way to do it unless he transfers them along with land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי אליעזר answers with a story of his own. This step sets up the story; the proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man could not easily do משיכה (pulling) on so much property. So the חכמים told him to use קנין אגב: transfer land, and the movables come along with it. This shows a real קנין was required.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
A man from the town of מרון

phrases.english: GEMARA:

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר לָהֶן רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לַחֲכָמִים:
phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita: Rabbi Eliezer said to the Sages:
There was an incident with a certain man from Meron who was in Jerusalem,
and he had a lot of movable property
and he wanted to give them as a gift.
They said to him: There is no way to fix this for them
unless he transfers them along with land.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר לָהֶן רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לַחֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the גמרא, where רבי אליעזר brings a counter-story to the חכמים' proof.
steps.raayaObject: That even a שכיב מרע needs a formal קנין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of the man from מרון (setup).

steps.title: The man from מרון transfers his property with land
steps.stepSummary: The man bought a rocky plot, gave its parts to people along with sheep and barrels, died, and the חכמים upheld it because it was done through a proper קנין.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went and bought a rocky plot near ירושלים and said: 'Its north side to so-and-so, and with it a hundred sheep and a hundred barrels; its south side to so-and-so, and with it a hundred sheep and a hundred barrels.' He died, and the חכמים upheld his words.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes רבי אליעזר's story. The man did a real קנין through land, and only then were his gifts upheld.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's point: if speech alone worked for a dying man, why bother buying land? The fact that a קנין was needed shows that words alone are not enough.

phrases.english: He went and acquired one rocky plot
near Jerusalem, and said:
Its north side to so-and-so,
and with it a hundred sheep and a hundred barrels;
and its south side to so-and-so,
and with it a hundred sheep and a hundred barrels.
And he died, and the Sages upheld his words.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָלַךְ וְלָקַח בֵּית סֶלַע אֶחָד סָמוּךְ לִירוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the story started in Step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That a dying person's gift needs a קנין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The man from מרון needed קנין אגב קרקע, and only then were his gifts upheld.

steps.title: The חכמים reject the proof: he was healthy
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer that the man from מרון was healthy, and a healthy person surely needs a קנין, so the story proves nothing about a dying person.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Is that a proof? The man from מרון was healthy!
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים knock down רבי אליעזר's proof. They point out that the man in the story was not on his deathbed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees a בריא (healthy person) needs a קנין. The debate is only about a שכיב מרע, so a case about a healthy man doesn't decide it.
steps.whatToRemember: Each side's story gets rejected. The בני רוכל case was special because of the sons, and the man from מרון was healthy.

phrases.english: They said to him: Is that a proof?!
The man from Meron was healthy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי אליעזר's proof from Steps 3 and 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the man from מרון.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The man was healthy, and the debate is only about a dying person.

steps.title: Why did רבי אליעזר curse the sons of Rokhel?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's curse again and asks what the sons did to deserve it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: 'The בני רוכל, may their mother bury them,' etc. Why was he cursing them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the curse in the משנה and asks for its reason. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה never says what the sons did wrong. The גמרא wants to know what made them deserve such a harsh curse.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc., the quote continues as in the משנה

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶן: בְּנֵי רוֹכֵל תִּקְבְּרֵם אִמָּן וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: He said to them: The sons of Rokhel, may their mother bury them, etc.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the line from the משנה (Step 2) so it can explain it.

phrases.english: What is the reason he was cursing them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה's curse from Step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What wrong the בני רוכל did that earned רבי אליעזר's curse.

steps.title: They kept thorns growing in a vineyard
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל answers that the בני רוכל let thorns grow in a vineyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: They kept thorns growing in a vineyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the sons were cursed because they let thorns grow in a vineyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Keeping thorns in a vineyard can be a problem of כלאי הכרם (forbidden mixed planting in a vineyard). The next step shows why רבי אליעזר saw this as a serious sin.

keyTerms.meaning: People who keep thorns growing (and don't uproot them)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
They were people who kept thorns growing in a vineyard,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: מְקַיְּימֵי קוֹצִים בַּכֶּרֶם הָיוּ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The בני רוכל kept thorns growing in a vineyard.

steps.title: This fits רבי אליעזר's view on thorns in a vineyard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows this matches רבי אליעזר's opinion in a משנה in כלאים: keeping thorns in a vineyard makes it forbidden. The חכמים disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר follows his own reasoning, as we learned: If someone keeps thorns in a vineyard, רבי אליעזר says the vineyard becomes forbidden. The חכמים say it does not become forbidden; only something people normally grow does that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up שמואל's answer. It shows that רבי אליעזר holds elsewhere that keeping thorns in a vineyard is a real כלאים sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר, the thorns made the vineyard forbidden, so the sons were real sinners and deserved the curse. The חכמים say thorns don't count, since people don't normally grow them on purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning from elsewhere
As we learned in a משנה
Something that people normally keep growing

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר cursed the בני רוכל because, in his view, their thorns made the vineyard forbidden as כלאים. This matches his opinion in מסכת כלאים.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer follows his own reasoning, as we learned:
One who keeps thorns growing in a vineyard,
Rabbi Eliezer says: He has made it forbidden;
phrases.notes: קדש here means the vineyard becomes forbidden because of כלאים, mixing plants in a vineyard.

phrases.english: and the Sages say: He has not made it forbidden,
only something that people normally keep growing does so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports שמואל's answer in Step 7 by showing it fits רבי אליעזר's known opinion.
steps.raayaObject: That keeping thorns in a vineyard is a serious sin in רבי אליעזר's eyes.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in כלאים, where רבי אליעזר says thorns in a vineyard make it forbidden.

steps.title: What are thorns good for?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אליעזר: saffron is useful, but thorns seem useless, so why should they forbid a vineyard?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that saffron is useful. But thorns, what are they good for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אליעזר's view from the last step that keeping thorns in a vineyard makes it forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plant forbids a vineyard as כלאים only if people grow it on purpose. Saffron fits that rule because it is useful. Thorns seem to be just weeds, so it is hard to see why רבי אליעזר treats them as a real crop.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (opens a contrast)

phrases.english: It makes sense that saffron is useful;
but thorns, what are they good for?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא כַּרְכּוֹם, חֲזֵי; אֶלָּא קוֹצִים, לְמַאי חֲזֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the רבי אליעזר opinion brought in step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's ruling that thorns forbid a vineyard
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only useful plants count as כלאים, and thorns seem useless

steps.title: In ערביא, thorns are grown for camels
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא explains that in ערביא people grow thorns as camel food, so thorns count as a useful plant.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: What is רבי אליעזר's reason? Because in ערביא people keep thorns in their fields for their camels.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא answers the challenge by showing that thorns are useful in at least one place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Thorns are not useless everywhere, because in ערביא they are grown on purpose to feed camels. רבי אליעזר holds that since some people grow thorns on purpose, thorns count as a real crop everywhere.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Eliezer?
Because in Arabia they keep thorns
in the fields for their camels.

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אליעזר, thorns forbid a vineyard because in some places, like ערביא, people grow them on purpose.
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the item really is useful in some places
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Thorns are worthless, so they should not count as a crop
steps.terutzMaskana: Thorns are grown on purpose in ערביא, so they count as useful

steps.title: A קנין may be done for a dying man even on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי rules that a קנין may be done for a שכיב מרע even on שבת. The reason is not רבי אליעזר's view that a קנין is required. It is to keep the dying man from getting upset.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי said: A קנין may be done for a dying person even on שבת. This is not because we worry about רבי אליעזר's opinion. It is so that he does not become upset and lose control of his mind.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי לוי gives a new rule: if a dying person asks for a קנין, we do it even on שבת. He then explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, business deals are not done on שבת. The הלכה does not follow רבי אליעזר, so a dying person's words work without a קנין. Still, if he asks for one, we do it, because seeing his wish ignored could upset him and make his condition worse.

keyTerms.meaning: A formal act that makes a transfer binding
A person who is dangerously ill / dying
To worry about / take into account
He will become very upset / lose control of his mind

steps.confusionAlert: רבי לוי does not mean a dying person needs a קנין. His words work even without one. We do the קנין only to calm him.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that protecting a dying person's peace of mind is important enough to allow a קנין even on שבת.

phrases.english: Rabbi Levi said:
We perform a kinyan from a dying person,
even on Shabbat.
And not because we worry about the words of Rabbi Eliezer,
phrases.notes: This is רבי אליעזר's view from earlier, that a dying person's gifts need a קנין.

phrases.english: but rather lest he become distraught.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי לֵוִי: קוֹנִין קִנְיָן מִשְּׁכִיב מְרַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the topic of a קנין for a dying person and gives a practical ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קנין is done for a שכיב מרע even on שבת, to keep him from distress, not because a קנין is required

steps.title: משנה: Do a dying person's spoken words count on שבת and on weekdays?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says a dying person's spoken words count only on שבת, since he cannot write then. רבי יהושע says that if they count on שבת, they surely count on a weekday.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבי אליעזר says: On שבת his words stand, because he cannot write; but not on a weekday. רבי יהושע says: If the חכמים said this about שבת, then all the more so on a weekday.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It brings a dispute about whether a dying person's spoken instructions are binding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that on a weekday the dying person can write, so his words alone are not enough. רבי יהושע turns this around: on שבת writing is forbidden and his words still count, so on a weekday, when writing is easier, his words surely count. For רבי יהושע, his words always count.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a weaker case to a stronger one: 'all the more so'

phrases.english: MISHNA: Rabbi Eliezer says:
On Shabbat, his words stand,
phrases.notes: "His" means the dying person's. His spoken instructions count.

phrases.english: because he cannot write;
but not on a weekday.
Rabbi Yehoshua says:
They said it about Shabbat; all the more so on a weekday.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: בַּשַּׁבָּת דְּבָרָיו קַיָּימִין
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: a dying person's words count only on שבת. רבי יהושע: they count on שבת and, all the more so, on a weekday.

steps.title: משנה: Acquiring on behalf of a minor or an adult
steps.stepSummary: In the same way, רבי אליעזר says one may acquire property on behalf of a minor but not on behalf of an adult. רבי יהושע says that if it works for a minor, it surely works for an adult.
steps.simpleTranslation: Similarly, one may acquire for a minor but not for an adult; these are the words of רבי אליעזר. רבי יהושע says: If they said it about a minor, then all the more so about an adult.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a second, parallel dispute between the same two תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that someone else may acquire on behalf of a minor, because the minor cannot do it himself. An adult can act for himself, so no one may acquire for him. רבי יהושע uses the same 'all the more so' reasoning as before: if it works for a minor, who cannot acquire on his own, it surely works for an adult, who can.
steps.whatToRemember: In both disputes, רבי אליעזר says the rule applies only where the person cannot act for himself. רבי יהושע argues 'all the more so' and applies the rule in both cases.

phrases.english: Similarly,
one may acquire for a minor, but one may not acquire for an adult;
these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.
Rabbi Yehoshua says:
They said it about a minor; all the more so about an adult.

steps.triggerLanguage: כַּיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ זָכִין לַקָּטָן וְאֵין זָכִין לַגָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel dispute between the same two תנאים, following the same pattern
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: acquiring on someone's behalf works only for a minor. רבי יהושע: all the more so for an adult.

steps.title: Whose opinion does the משנה follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens its discussion by asking which תנא's view the משנה is written according to.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Whose view is our משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא section begins, and its first question is which sage the משנה follows. This is a setup question; the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה presented רבי אליעזר saying a dying man's spoken words count only on שבת, when he cannot write. The גמרא asks this because there turns out to be more than one report of what רבי אליעזר said, so it wants to know whose report the משנה follows.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion of the משנה that follows it
Our משנה, the one we just learned

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Our mishna, whose view is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's discussion of the משנה whose ruling was summarized in Step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which sage's version of רבי אליעזר's view the משנה is written according to.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is the view of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a short answer: the משנה follows רבי יהודה. The proof comes right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer names רבי יהודה even though the משנה itself spoke in the name of רבי אליעזר. That means the גמרא is saying the משנה uses רבי יהודה's report of what רבי אליעזר held, and not someone else's report.

keyTerms.meaning: It is the view of רבי יהודה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי יהודה is replacing רבי אליעזר. The משנה still quotes רבי אליעזר. The question is only whose report of רבי אליעזר's words the משנה is using.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי יהודה's report of רבי אליעזר's view.

steps.title: רבי מאיר quotes רבי אליעזר the opposite way
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי מאיר reported רבי אליעזר as saying a dying man's spoken words count on a weekday but not on שבת. That is the reverse of the משנה, so the משנה is not following רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי מאיר says that רבי אליעזר says: On a weekday his words stand, because he can write, but not on שבת. רבי יהושע...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove its answer. In it, רבי מאיר reports רבי אליעזר's view in the opposite way from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי אליעזר said spoken words count only on שבת, because the man cannot write then. In רבי מאיר's report, the words count only on a weekday, 'because he can write', and not on שבת. Because this is the reverse of the משנה, the משנה must follow the other report, the one by רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא
Because he is able to write

steps.whatToRemember: There are two reports of רבי אליעזר's view. In the משנה's version (רבי יהודה), spoken words count only on שבת. In רבי מאיר's version, they count only on a weekday.
steps.confusionAlert: The reason is the same in both versions, whether he is able to write, but it leads to opposite results. Watch which day each version says the words count.
